120.0.s.en: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

120.0.0.en: 1- The psalmist suffers severe distress, so that he cried out to God, and what he offered was not merely an ordinary prayer or petition, but he enjoys great faith, so that he believed that God had answered him even though the answer had not yet appeared. Yet he trusts in God's answer, which gave him inner peace, because he relies on a previous spiritual experience with God, who rescued him from many sufferings.

120.0.1.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ in the midst of His sufferings and His endurance of the Cross, for He trusts that His prayer will be answered, whether in the Garden of Gethsemane or on the Cross, and that He will redeem mankind and rise from the dead, proclaiming His victory over sin for our sake.

120.1.0.en: 1- The psalmist marvels at the man with the deceitful, lying tongue, for what does he gain from this evil and hypocrisy, and from his persistence in this deceit, which must lead him to eternal destruction? By the one with the deceitful tongue is meant Satan, and every wicked person who follows Satan. The torment that awaits the liar is not only at the end of his life, but also deceit and trickery torment their possessor, for he feels a division and duplicity within himself, so that he is troubled and has no peace; and even if the deceiver thinks that by his lying he obtains some of the material things of the world, these are passing away.

120.1.1.en: 2- At the beginning of the spiritual path, when a person tries to ascend to God, for this is the first of the psalms of ascents, that is, the first step on the way of spiritual striving, when a person decides to live with God, the demons gather around him with their deceptions. They praise him and entice him with lusts, hoping that he will fall into pride or defilement, and so be hindered from ascending to God.

120.1.2.en: 3- These verses are also a prophecy about Christ and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Him with a deceitful kiss, and in hypocrisy showed himself as a friend of Christ.

120.2.0.en: (Juniper: a kind of wormwood tree found in deserts such as the desert of the Arabian Peninsula, called the "ar'ar", from which charcoal is made, distinguished by its intense heat and the long time it stays alight.

120.2.1.en: 1- The psalmist likens the wicked deceivers to sharp arrows of a mighty man, with which they wish to kill those who offend them, and he also likens them to a fire blazing fiercely to burn those around them; but the righteous, the children of God, take refuge in Him, so the offenses of these wicked people do not reach them.

120.2.2.en: 2- The wicked liars will receive severe torment, which he likens to sharp, strong arrows and a fiercely burning fire, so that their torment will be very painful.

120.2.3.en: 3- On the other hand, St. Augustine sees that the sharp arrows are the arrows of the word of God that prick the wicked and lead them to repentance, and the coals of juniper are the fire of the Holy Spirit, which burns their sins away through repentance and kindles their love toward God.

120.2.4.en: Do not be affected by the deceit and trickery that surround you in the world, but take refuge in God through prayer, that He may establish you in His commandments, so that you are not swept along with the current of evil, and are not disturbed by the deceit of the wicked, but live in peace through the strength of your faith.

120.3.0.en: (Mesech: they are the descendants of Japheth the son of Noah (Gen 10:2), tribes who dwelt to the north-east of the land of the Jews and worked in trade; they represent the people of the world who are far from God and preoccupied with material things. Kedar: the second son of Ishmael, tribes who roamed the Arabian Peninsula and were distinguished by violence and fierceness, and who lived in tents made of black goat skin, so their tents are a symbol of darkness and evil.

120.3.1.en: 1- The psalmist declares his distress at dwelling, not among the tribes of Mesech or the tribes of Kedar, but among wicked people who resemble the tribes of Mesech, far from God, or the tribes of Kedar, full of evil and violence. Therefore he felt his estrangement from those around him, and sought God's help to reassure him and surround him with His love.

120.3.2.en: 2- The spiritual person who walks by God's commandments feels like a stranger in the midst of the world, because of the conduct of those around him in evil, deceit and lying, so he asks God's help to deliver him from this distress of soul, to support him with His love, and to restore his peace to him.

120.4.0.en: 1- Although the psalmist feels estranged among the wicked people of the world, who are occupied with deceit and lying, he held fast to God and His commandments, and God granted him an unshakable peace.

120.4.1.en: 2- He held fast to peace and love, so they could not bear his words, and insisted on making war with others, and with him too. Yet he was not troubled, because God protects him and establishes him in peace and love toward them and toward all people.

120.4.2.en: 3- This verse is a prophecy about Christ, who is the God of peace, and who endured His opponents and enemies who tried to trap Him in a word, and reviled Him, and tried to kill Him, but He remained loving them and died for their sake.

120.4.3.en: Be firm in your faith in God, and ask His help to live in peace however much the wicked provoke you. Do not act with violence and harshness in response to their offenses, and be confident that your love extinguishes the flame of evil and remains a light for the world.

120.4.4.en: The Lord is the Helper and the Keeper. A song of ascents: "I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help" (v. 1). Introduction:

120.4.5.en: 1- Its author: the title of the psalm gives no name for its author, so it is one of the orphan psalms whose author is not known.

120.4.6.en: 2- This psalm was recited on the second step, after the preceding psalm, during the ascent, for it is one of the songs of ascents, as the title states.

120.4.7.en: 3- After the preceding psalm showed the estrangement of the spiritual person who seeks God, this psalm shows God who helps His children and keeps them in all their steps. It is therefore suitable for everyone in distress, or who expects distress to come upon him, so that his faith in God may be established.

120.4.8.en: 4- This is a liturgical psalm; those going up used to chant it antiphonally among the groups ascending: one group chants (vv. 1, 2), then another group chants (vv. 3, 4), and after this they chant vv. 5-8.

120.4.9.en: 5- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Vespers, where the worshiper lifts his eyes to God before the sun of his life sets, asking His help and His keeping in the remaining hours before he sleeps, not only on this night, but for the rest of the days of his life.

121.0.0.en: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

121.0.1.en: 1- The one going up to Jerusalem and its temple would lift his eyes to the mountain that rises toward heaven, where dwells God who is able to help a person in all his steps, so that he is strengthened and endures the pains and weariness of the ascent.

121.0.2.en: 2- The mountain is a symbol of the saints who rise with their lives to heaven; they are an example for us through their lives, that we may imitate them, and so find God's help in our lives as they did.

121.0.3.en: 3- The mountain is a symbol of Christ the Mighty and Powerful, who came down from heaven to lift us up on high through faith in Him, and through His help.

121.1.0.en: My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth.

121.1.1.en: 1- The psalmist feels that his help comes from the Lord, the Creator of heaven and earth, in whose hand is everything, and it is not right to look to anyone but Him, because He is the Almighty. A person's help is from God, and even if He allows someone to help a person, it is God who works through him.

121.1.2.en: 2- When the children of Israel sinned, and worshiped idols, and drew far from God, and were preoccupied with lusts, they entered the distress of captivity; and when they returned to God, He brought them back from captivity, because God alone is the Helper.

121.1.3.en: The more you lift up your eyes to heaven and trust in God, the more you gradually rise above earthly lusts and the cares of this world, and then you receive inner peace, in addition to abundant blessings.

121.2.0.en: He will not suffer your foot to be moved: he that keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he that keeps Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.

121.2.1.en: 1- God keeps you so that you do not slip, and what is meant by slipping is falling and persisting in the fall, that is, not repenting. This comes from pride, or its opposite, smallness of soul, which leads to despair.

121.2.2.en: But as for the one who repents, however much he slips and falls, the compassionate God receives him. The one who believes in God and trusts in Him does not remain in slipping or despair, because he looks to the Lord his keeper, who rescues him however much he falls.

121.2.3.en: 2- The Lord differs from all people in that He neither slumbers nor sleeps, whereas all people, however great their strength or their love for you, are weak; they slumber and are heedless of you, and cannot keep you. Therefore it is folly to depend on them, but the Lord is the keeper of Israel, that is, the keeper of His people; He alone is able to keep you.

121.3.0.en: The Lord is your keeper: the Lord is your shade upon your right hand.

121.3.1.en: 1- The Lord shades a person during afflictions and helps him in them; these are symbolized by the scorching rays of the sun. And He shades the striving person if he falls, to raise him up and let him repent. By this shade He shows tenderness to His children, as a hen has tenderness for her chicks, to encourage them in their spiritual striving.

121.3.2.en: 2- He shades the right hand, which is a symbol of good works, namely the prayers lifted up before God, works of goodness, and every spiritual service; so He encourages His children in them and supports them against the schemes of the devil.

121.3.3.en: 3- If the shadow of Peter healed the sick (Acts 5:15), how much more does the shadow of Christ heal and support in all spiritual and bodily sicknesses.

121.4.0.en: The sun shall not smite you by day, nor the moon by night.

121.4.1.en: 1- God, who keeps His children, keeps them from the strokes of the sun, which symbolizes trials and the open wars of Satan; God supports His children and repels these attacks from them, so long as they hold fast to Him and seek His help.

121.4.2.en: 2- The Lord also keeps His children from the strokes of the moon, for it is said that the light of the moon harms those who dwell in the deserts if they are not careful. The strokes of the moon are a symbol of the cunning, deceptive strokes of Satan, and of every sin committed in the dark for fear of the eyes of people. In sum, God protects His children night and day, and throughout their lives, because they have trusted in Him.

121.5.0.en: The Lord shall preserve you from all evil: he shall preserve your soul.

121.5.1.en: The Lord keeps His children from every evil, great or small, and keeps their souls in faith in Him, firm in His commandments; even if He does not remove the affliction, He gives them grace, and they experience Him deeply during the affliction. Indeed, His work shines forth with power if He allows the affliction to remain, as He kept the three youths inside the furnace: He did not quench it, but appeared to them and walked with them, and they praised Him.

121.6.0.en: The Lord shall preserve your going out and your coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.

121.6.1.en: 1- The Lord keeps your entering into the world and your going out from it, that is, He keeps you throughout your life.

121.6.2.en: And He keeps you also at your entering into the Church through Baptism, and keeps your going out to the Kingdom of Heaven. Likewise He keeps you in your going out from the lusts of the world and your entering into a deep relationship with God, which begins now and continues forever in heaven.

121.6.3.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ in His entering into the world by the Incarnation and His going out by the Resurrection and the Ascension.

121.6.4.en: If the Lord keeps you in all the stages of your life, and throughout your lifetime, then be at ease and cast your care upon Him, that you may enjoy His care and be free to meditate on Him and to enjoy His fellowship.

121.6.5.en: Joy in Jerusalem, the house of the Lord. A song of ascents of David: "I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord" (v. 1). Introduction:

121.6.6.en: 1- Its author: the prophet David, as the title of this psalm states.

121.6.7.en: 2- This psalm shows David's love, and his heart's attachment to the house of the Lord and to worship in it.

121.6.8.en: 3- This psalm is a prophecy about the feelings of those returning from captivity to Jerusalem to build the temple and restore worship in the house of the Lord, of which they had been deprived throughout the period of captivity.

121.6.9.en: 4- The house of the Lord in Jerusalem is a symbol of the Church of the New Testament, and also of the heavenly Jerusalem.

121.6.10.en: 5- This psalm is prayed on the third step at the ascent to the house of the Lord.

121.6.11.en: 6- This psalm shows the importance of common prayer and worship (v. 4).

121.6.12.en: 7- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Vespers, where the worshiper remembers the house of the Lord and the worship in it, that his heart may be lifted up to heaven, where the eternal home with God is. For when the day draws near its end, we remember that we are approaching eternal life, and so we prepare with many prayers and praise.

122.0.s.en: (1) Joy in the house of the Lord

122.0.0.en: I was glad when they said unto me, "Let us go into the house of the Lord."

122.0.1.en: 1- A person rejoices in the one who encourages him to go to the house of the Lord, if he is repentant, or loves God and wants to be present before Him in His house to praise Him and thank Him.

122.0.2.en: 2- God's angels rejoice over us when we desire to go to the house of the Lord as they do.

122.0.3.en: 3- The joy of going to the house of the Lord is a longing for common prayer, and a faith in God's blessing in His house, which is distinguished from His blessing in every other place.

122.1.0.en: Our feet shall stand within your gates, O Jerusalem.

122.1.1.en: David imagines that he has completed the ascent to Jerusalem and stands before its gates, and this gives him a joy surpassing every joy, because he has reached the city of God and its temple, that is, he will enter into the presence of God and enjoy being in His hands. There he offers his repentance for all his sins, shows his love in songs of praise, and shares with his brethren in worship.

122.2.0.en: Jerusalem is built as a city that is compact together.

122.2.1.en: 1- David feels that Jerusalem is like a city joined together, one part to another, meaning the unity of the believers who worship God in the temple of Jerusalem, so that they pray before Him with one heart.

122.2.2.en: 2- This is a prophecy about the oneness of the believers in the Church of the New Testament, where they become members in the Body of Christ, and He is the Head. This oneness appears even more clearly in the heavenly Jerusalem, where the believers are united in praising the risen Christ in their midst.

122.3.0.en: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord. For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.

122.3.2.en: 1- The tribes of Israel, that is, all the believers, come to worship in Jerusalem, especially at the three great feasts: the Passover, Pentecost, and Tabernacles. All are believers who love to worship God, and each tribe is distinct from the others, yet in unity they stand before God. Also in Jerusalem they go to law before the judges who know the Law, who sit on the thrones of judgment, and King David and his descendants sit among these judges.

122.3.3.en: 2- Here he prophesies about the gathering of the believers in the Church to worship and give thanks to God, and to submit to its teaching and the guidance of its priests, who sit on the thrones of guidance and judgment.

122.3.4.en: 3- He also prophesies about the gathering of the believers in the Kingdom of Heaven and on the day of judgment, when the twelve disciples will sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes who did not believe in Christ, and to live with Him.

122.3.5.en: 4- The thrones may mean the hearts of the believers in which God sits and rests to lead their lives, and to warn them by the Holy Spirit to keep away from sin, and He judges them, rebukes them and convicts them so that they may rise from it.

122.3.6.en: And so He leads them in the way of life to the Kingdom.

122.3.7.en: How beautiful it is to be present before God in His house! So take courage with your brethren to be before Him as much as you can, that you may enjoy not only His presence, but also partaking of His Body and Blood.

122.4.0.en: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: may they rest that love you. Peace be within your towers, rest within your palaces.

122.4.1.en: 1- Since judgment was established in Jerusalem by the Law of God, discipline and peace pervaded the city, and consequently those who love Jerusalem gained rest for dwelling in it and worshiping God; rest for all, whether those dwelling in it on towers in the mountains, or those dwelling in Jerusalem in palaces, that is, great houses.

122.4.2.en: 2- Here he prophesies about the Church of the New Testament, and asks peace for it, as we now pray and ask in the litany for the peace of the Church in the Divine Liturgy. The towers are the saints, for they are like towers in their high spiritual rank, and are like towers also in their security, because they are under God's protection. The palaces are the true believers, who are temples of the Holy Spirit and palaces in which God the King dwells. And the palaces are a symbol of the abundance of good things in them, just as Christ gives abundant spiritual and material good things to His children.

122.5.0.en: For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say, "Peace be within you." Because of the house of the Lord our God I will seek your good.

122.5.1.en: 1- David asks peace for Jerusalem for the sake of his relatives and friends, that is, all the Jews who dwell in Jerusalem and those who visit it, so that they may enjoy worship in a tranquil atmosphere. Indeed he also asks goodness and blessings for Jerusalem, because the house of the Lord is in it, for God sanctifies His city by dwelling in it.

122.5.2.en: 2- These verses are a prophecy about Christ, who asks peace for His Church for the sake of His brethren, since He is the firstborn among many brethren, and asks good for it, because it is His house in which He dwells.

122.5.3.en: May you pray for the peace of the Church, and the peace of all around you, that they may live with God in holy worship; and do not forget yourself, but ask for your own inner peace, so that you may be able to behold God.

122.5.4.en: Taking refuge in God in affliction. A song of ascents: "Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens" (v. 1). Introduction:

122.5.5.en: 1- Its author: it is one of the orphan psalms in which the name of the psalmist is not mentioned.

122.5.6.en: 2- The words of the psalm show the author's faith in God and his taking refuge in Him, especially as he is exposed to distresses from those around him. It suits every believer who suffers distresses, for the psalm is a prayer of supplication to the merciful God.

122.5.7.en: 3- This psalm is prayed on the fourth of the steps of the ascent to the temple of the Lord.

122.5.8.en: 4- This psalm may be a prophecy about the feelings of Nehemiah when he visited Jerusalem and saw the walls broken down and the gates burned; he began to rebuild them, and his enemies around him rose against him, mocked him, and tried to oppose him by every means.

122.5.9.en: 5- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Vespers, because it suits the worshiper at the end of the day as he implores God to deliver him from the wars of the demons that confronted him throughout the day, so that they may quiet down for him at the end of the day and during the night.
